query: I'm building a support chatbot that answers from our help center docs. What should I eval?
note: Specific grounded support bot. Retrieval, faithfulness, known-answer probes, and a judge are the direct checks.

query: A coding agent that writes pull requests and runs the test suite before it asks for review.
note: Specific coding agent. Grade by running the code, checking the trajectory, and using a second model as reviewer.

query: An assistant that books meetings on my calendar by emailing the other person and writing the invite.
note: Specific tool-using agent. Tool checks, the path it takes, how much it does alone, and whether the meeting actually gets booked.

query: A classifier that routes incoming support tickets to the right team.
note: Specific router. Routing accuracy is the direct metric, with query classification and false-route rates beside it.

query: We summarize sales calls into CRM notes and need to know when the notes invent quotes.
note: Specific note generator. Check quotes against the call, flag invented facts, and compare note variants.

query: RAG search over our internal docs. I want to know if the retriever finds the right pages before the model answers.
note: Specific RAG pipeline. Score retrieval on its own, then each step, then whether the answer stays on the docs.

query: A bot that reviews pull requests and leaves comments on the diff.
note: Specific review bot. A second-model critique, running the code, and whether people accept the comments.

query: A proactive assistant that pings me to prep for a meeting. I need the ping rate to be trustworthy.
note: Specific proactive nudges. False alarms, whether people dismiss them, and whether prep actually happens.

query: Our agent can read private customer records and send email. How do I eval the chance it leaks data?
note: Specific exfiltration risk. The private-data plus outbound-action check, runtime blocks, and a broader safety pass.

query: I wrote an LLM judge for support-answer quality and need to know if it agrees with human raters.
note: Specific judge validation. Human TPR/TNR, the judge prompt itself, and a bias audit.

query: Our chatbot agrees with the user even when the user is wrong. I want that caught before each release.
note: Specific sycophancy failure. A per-release score and a judge bias audit that includes sycophancy.

query: We are A/B testing a new ranker for search over our docs and need to know if it actually helps.
note: Specific ranker experiment. Online outcomes, the A/B itself, and recall if the ranker is the retriever.

query: An expense agent takes many steps from receipt to filed report. I need to see which step it breaks on.
note: Specific multi-step agent. The failure matrix, the full trajectory, trace coding, and per-step checks.

query: When a new model drops I want a private benchmark of our real tasks, not a public leaderboard.
note: Specific model-swap decision. A private task set, a backlog of failures, and more than one way to compare models.

query: Users can thumbs-down any AI answer. I want those complaints turned into eval cases.
note: Specific feedback loop. Capture the thumb, turn the complaint into a case, then rank the themes.

query: Prompt changes should fail CI if they regress bugs we already fixed.
note: Specific regression gate. A golden set in CI, built from labeled must-not-fail cases.

query: A public chatbot needs a filter for toxic and off-tone replies before users see them.
note: Specific safety filter. Toxicity detection, blocking on the request path, and a red-team set.

query: An IDE copilot suggests the next lines of code. I want to know if developers actually accept them.
note: Specific inline completions. Acceptance rate, how stable a suggestion is across samples, and whether the code runs.

query: Our support bot is multi-turn. When it fails I can't tell a memory bug from a missing article.
note: Specific multi-turn diagnosis. Replay the session as a single turn, simulate the user, and code the traces.

query: Clinicians should write the rubric we use to grade medical answers from the model.
note: Specific expert grading. A clinician rubric, expert review of real tasks, and expert-written failures.

query: Start the email agent on drafts, log every human edit, and only let it send once the edits get rare.
note: Specific autonomy rollout. The ladder, a staged release, and a resolution rate once it sends on its own.

query: A safety score that looks good because the agent refuses everything is not a real improvement.
note: Specific safety gaming. Pair a progress metric with safety so standing still does not count as safe.

query: Every week we throw vague, wrong, and hostile questions at the bot and write down where it breaks.
note: Specific probing ritual. A weekly break-it pass, generated edge cases, and questions we can check in the source.

query: For a shopping assistant I want the eval set to be the product requirements, not a slide deck.
note: Specific product process. Evals as the PRD, choosing which evals to build, and watching real shoppers.

query: Sample live production traces, judge them, and turn the failures into new eval cases.
note: Specific production loop. Monitor live traces, feed failures back into the set, and keep calibrating.
